selectionRule.freeRunClock: WAIT: step 3's free-run clock as question 19 was answered (ADR-089:5): down linemen run from their snap spot (depth 1.0, width his gap, EDGE +0.75), every other free runner keeps today's set times (ADR-089:558)

loss.population: aimed throws on both sides (pass attempts not charted as throwaways)
loss.clock: raw-second bins read from THROW.releaseSeconds (P8, from step 4)
loss.weightsSource: the real share of attempts by raw-second bin (ADR-089:181), the same for every grid point
loss.normalise: each curve divided by its own all-bin mean: the unweighted mean of its seven bin rates
loss.formula: sum_i w_i (s_i / mean(s) - r_i / mean(r))^2 / sum_i w_i
loss.shapeOnly: the level is left out on purpose, so that hits on thrown balls per dropback stay a prediction (ADR-089:422)
loss.reproduces: 0.0034 between ADR-089:169 and :171 on their printed bins, against K1's REPORTED 0.0035 (ADR-089:173)
loss.winner: the least loss on seed set 1, over all 14 points of both shapes
loss.ties: the earlier point in the filed order: S by theta ascending, then L by R ascending
loss.rerun: once, mechanically, at step 10 after b, the throwaway appeal and the situation weights are fitted (fittingOrder)
loss.notOn: sacks (post hoc in the ADR-061 sense) and ESPN (no league average; entry 125) (ADR-089:426)

separation.rule: no separation if worst - best <= 2 * max_g spread_g, best and worst on seed set 1, over all 14 points

fallback.population: attempts, throwaways counted as throws on both sides (ADR-089:188)
fallback.rule: the same loss, separation statistic and winner rule
fallback.ledger: the pressured-by-release curve moves out of the falsifiers and into the fitted ledger, and the report says so
fallback.ifNotSeparatedEither: the design states no further step: the fallback's minimum stands and its separation is reported

steps: 1. step 5a: the three read-system budget deltas, on the clean bench, which sees no line
2. step 5b: the block clock, by the filed selection rule, with b at its provisional 5
3. step 10: b, fitted to the league sack share of hit-or-sack, 44.6%, on its filed grid
4. step 10: the throwaway appeal, fitted to 3.54% overall and 8.84% pressured
6. step 10: the block clock selection re-run once, mechanically, with those three fixed (b moves hits between release bins)
7. step 10: if the selection changes, b is refitted once on the new clock and the process stops; both passes are reported
fittingOrder.ownerReturn: If the second pass would change the selection again, the design comes back to the owner (ADR-089:1128).

clauses.row: what fails means
clauses.text: Acceptance fails if any graded row is outside its band on the generated league, or any falsifier is outside its filed band, or the interception guard is broken. Nothing is retuned to make a failed row pass without a new filed prediction. A miss is classed and taken to the owner by the miss rule. An accepted miss is still a miss: under option B the row stays failed in the ledger unless the owner rules by name that it passes.

clauses.row: pressured share of 2.0 s throws, raw seconds

clauses.text: The class, by a split filed in advance and measured on the arm that missed (missRule.ts classifyMiss).

clauses.row: class (i), supply

clauses.row: class (ii), timing
clauses.text: (ii) Timing: the bin fails without a free runner, the quick share fails with no free runner, or free runners arrive earlier than M8's table.

clauses.row: class (iii), conversion
clauses.text: (iii) Conversion: hit-or-sack in its band but sacks or the share short.

clauses.row: class (iv), unclassed
clauses.text: (iv) Unclassed: a covered row misses with none of (i) to (iii) holding; where two classes hold on different rows, both are named.

clauses.row: what happens next
clauses.text: What happens next goes to the owner, never automatically, with the class and the options, each priced on two seed sets.

clauses.row: option A
clauses.text: A. A protection design, first as an information arm, then as its own design with its own petitions.

clauses.row: option B
clauses.text: B. Accept and report: a named, accepted miss; acceptance has not passed while it stands, unless the owner rules by name that it passes.

clauses.row: option C
clauses.text: C. The owner revisits who counts as completely unblocked (D19, reading (b), against reading (c)); reading (a) is never offered.

clauses.row: class (iii)'s next suppliers
clauses.text: For a class (iii) miss the named next suppliers are, in order: question 8's rescoring (step 6); question 7's checklist at the deadline (step 6); the won-rep half of the alarm (step 7); step 8b's situation term.

clauses.row: the stop rule
clauses.text: One pass of the options per step. If the chosen option misses again, the step stops and the design comes back to the owner.

A rise beyond it stops the step and comes back to the owner with the numbers, including a second seed set.

clauses.text: The additive mix rule applied to each class separately (normal-bar pocket throws, rank-pushed, checkdowns, clean-expiry throws at 30, must-act desperation in a dirty pocket, throws on the run); a fall in one class never offsets a rise in another. A breach stops the step and goes to the owner with a second seed set.

m1Bound.definition: B1 = E + 3 * SD, with E = sum P and SD = sqrt(sum P(1 - P)) over dropbacks (deviation O1); the hard bound H = the number of such dropbacks; B1 in points = 100 * B1 / dropbacks

E.note: the expected count of dropbacks the window adds

H.note: dropbacks with a 1-14 POWER rep released at 1.0 s or later

dropbacks.note: the corpus's dropbacks, the denominator of B1 in points

margins1to4.note: E, SD, B1 and H for margins 1 to 4, counted apart

margins5to14.note: E, SD, B1 and H for margins 5 to 14

uses.text: Step 1's falsifier: the window alone moves pressure by at most B1 (in points), and sacks by at most 0.3 (s1.window.pressure, s1.window.sack).
The S band's upper pressure edge, raised by B1 in points: 40 + B1 (s1.S.pressure).
5b's upper pressure edge, raised by B1 in points: 42 + B1 (s5b.pressure).

step3Check.part1: The build does what the design says (this step's falsifier; a failure is a build fault): every free runner's published etaTick equals M8's function (deviation O2) for his snap row, ratings and drop, applied to that play's own PLAY_START and snapshot, to the tenth, by origin and snap row, under question 19's answer (Wait) and with the Mug arm off; a faster or quicker-accelerating man is never later; a deeper drop never brings him sooner; the same seed gives the same stream; the mirror guard holds (s3.part1.*). The base table is not the check: games diverge from step 1, so the step-3 stream's free runners are not the base seasons' men.
step3Check.part2: The real rows, on the pricing arm and the design build, reported against their bands, a miss going to the owner under the miss rule: the 2.0 s tick bin (limit 29.4), hit-or-sack, the quick-pressure share (30 to 55) and its origin, completely unblocked pressures per 100 dropbacks (at most 14) and their share of hit-or-sack (at most 40 in 100), with completely unblocked men per 100 dropbacks reported beside them (s3.*). A late block, a uniform delay or a refit of the free-run constants is never offered for a man nobody touched.

freeRun.tauSlope.unit: seconds per point of Acceleration - Speed

freeRun.getOffSeconds.unit: seconds (0 for a man already moving)

value.informationOnly: question 19 was answered Wait: only the down lineman's row is built (M8); the rest is information

safetyCreeping.start: already moving at 3 yd/s, no reaction

snap.tableNow.unit: yards; depth off the ball, width from the centre

arrivalReading.text: Default D21, filed at step 0 and never chosen by a fit: for the throwing motion, a free runner reaches him at his free-run time in tenths; a beaten blocker's man reaches him at his breaking time T_j plus his travel, not at his published arrival on the half-second grid; under shape L the breaking time is L's crossing time. This is a race between the throw and the hit only: with the ball still in his hand, contact resolves on the half-second grid, as today. RUSH_THREAT.etaTick keeps its documented meaning; the continuous time lives only on QB_HIT. The half-second reading runs as information only, and switching readings to pass a row is never allowed (ADR-089:1040).

params.lateBlock: the late block's breaking or crossing time + his travel (ADR-089:546)
params.heldBall: contact on the half-second grid, as today

lCrossingTime.text: Under shape L a won rep's continuous time is its crossing time, interpolated within the tick from its two reported margins: T_L = (t - 0.5) + 0.5 * (15 - m(t - 0.5)) / (m(t) - m(t - 0.5)), clamped to (t - 0.5, t], where t is the first tick at which the margin reaches 15 (RUSHER_WINS_REP); m(0) = 0, which follows from min(1, 0/R) = 0. His arrival is T_L plus his travel, so both shapes are scored on the same reading.

params.t: the first tick whose margin reaches 15

lateBlock.text: The late block on both shapes, for a man somebody got a hand on only (RAN_THROUGH, LATE_EXCHANGE; default D19). Its rep margin is the touching CHECK's margin turned round, m = -(margin) of the blitz_pickup or stunt_communication CHECK, so 1 to 19. Shape S: T = t_e + w * theta * exp(-beta * m/41) * E^(1/k), w the weak-block multiplier, E drawn on fork beat/<rollRef> where rollRef is that CHECK's rngLabel, published as a pass_rush_beat CHECK (P2). Shape L: round(min(1, (t - t_e)/(w * R)) * (m + jitter_t)), the jitter drawn each tick on .../t<tick>/<rusherId>:late. Once beaten, his threat is built as a won rep's is, and D21 reads his time as the shape's breaking or crossing time plus that travel. Its dials t_e and w stay CHOSEN.

params.margin: m = -(margin of the touching CHECK), 1 to 19
params.shapeS: T = t_e + w * theta * exp(-beta * m/41) * E^(1/k); E on beat/<rollRef of the touching CHECK>
params.shapeL: round(min(1, (t - t_e) / (w * R)) * (m + jitter_t)); jitter on .../t<tick>/<rusherId>:late
params.arrival: D21: breaking or crossing time + travel

missRule.text: The miss rule (default D31), filed at step 0, before step 3 runs, respecting the owner's question-4 words in every branch (ADR-089:1170-1185). It covers step 3's real rows, step 5b's and acceptance's graded rows, and the free-run clock's four rows. A miss is classed by the split filed here, measured on the arm that missed, and taken to the owner with its class and the options, each priced on two seed sets; nothing in it is automatic. One pass of the options per step; if the chosen option misses again, the step stops and the design comes back to the owner.
classes: (i) Supply: the 2.0 s bin passes on dropbacks without a free runner, but free runners are on more than (L - n)/(100 - n) of the 2.0 s throws; or completely unblocked pressures exceed 14 per 100 dropbacks; or their share of hit-or-sack exceeds 40 in 100; or the quick-pressure share fails while it passes on pressured dropbacks with no free runner. That points to protection.

(ii) Timing: the bin fails on dropbacks without a free runner, the quick-pressure share fails on pressured dropbacks with no free runner, or free runners arrive earlier than M8's table. That points to the block clock or the count, or to a build fault.
(iii) Conversion: hit-or-sack is in its band but sacks or the share are short. That points to contact, the hold and the outs.
(iv) Unclassed: a covered row that misses with none of (i) to (iii) holding goes to the owner labelled unclassed, with its numbers, the same options and the same stop rule.
options: A. A protection design: fewer blown pickups and missed stunt exchanges, first as an information arm, then as its own design with its own petitions.
B. Accept and report: the row is recorded in the ledger as a named, accepted miss and the build goes on; acceptance has not passed while it stands, unless the owner rules by name that it passes.
C. The owner revisits who counts as 'completely unblocked' (D19, reading (b), against reading (c)); reading (a) is never offered.
neverMoves: the free-run constants (D18, D22; and the snap-spot table if question 19 is answered Table now)
the reading of 'completely unblocked' (D19), unless the owner changes it under option C
no completely unblocked man is ever timed as a late block or by a uniform delay, whatever the row

params.classIFormula: (L - n) / (100 - n), in percent of the 2.0 s throws

L.rule: the tick grid at step 3; raw seconds once the motion exists (step 4 on)

params.n: pressured_share_2s_no_free_runner, measured on each arm, never chosen (ADR-089:1132), printed beside each arm
params.pricedOn: two seed sets (base.corpora, seed sets 1 and 2)
conversionSuppliers: the won-rep half of the alarm (step 7)
params.bothNamed: where two classes hold on different rows, both are named
params.stop: one pass of the options per step; a second miss stops the step and returns the design to the owner

bGrid.text: The contest's sack boundary b starts at 5 (resultTierLadder's SUCCESS boundary) and is fitted at step 10 to the league sack share of 44.6%, on the grid of the whole numbers -15 to 15 (deviation O6: the lower edge effectively sets step 10's sack level, because a lower b means more sacks). Its unit test is the closed form P(d100 - d100 >= b) = (100 - b)(101 - b)/20000 for b >= 1 (0.456 at b = 5) and 1 - (99 + b)(100 + b)/20000 for b <= 0 (0.505 at b = 0). Its reachable range is filed as REPORTED stand-ins (ADR-089:671), measured at the grid's ends at steps 4 and 10, reported beside the fit, and the grid is never widened to reach 44.6 (ADR-089:1123).

reachableRange.unit: sack share of hit-or-sack, %, with every contact a sack (the stand-in ceiling; REPORTED, TOT §8.3)
reachableRange.how: measured at the grid's ends (b = -15 and b = 15) on the step's build, reported beside the fit
reachableRange.neverWidened: the grid is never widened to reach 44.6 (ADR-089:1123)

runMargin.text: At the pursuit deadline RUN (today's escape terms, Mobility/1.5 + Improvisation/1.5, +5 an urgency step) is ranked against THROWAWAY (today's throwaway appeal, 25 + Decision Making/3 + Awareness/4, +8 an urgency step). RUN's base is the throwaway appeal's base plus Δ = 10, which moves with that base when step 10 fits it: the smallest whole margin at which a quarterback at the 70 baseline ranks RUN strictly first at every urgency 0 to 3 (deviation O7). Step 10 re-checks it as a structural row, a baseline quarterback in a neutral situation ranking RUN first at the deadline, and a failure comes back to the owner. If step 6's deadline pick reads a different urgency range, Δ is re-derived by the same inequality as a named amendment (risk K9).

params.inequality: Δ + 5u > 8u for every u in 0..3, so Δ > 9
params.ties: strict: a tie is not RUN first (the deadline pick's tie order is not built until step 6)
params.noClimbLaneBonus: not applied: the deadline follows a break-out, outside the pocket

unblockedBands.text: Completely unblocked pressures at most 14 per 100 dropbacks (twice PFF's about 7) and their share of hit-or-sack at most 40 in 100 (twice PFF's about 20), CHOSEN at an assumed 22,000 dropbacks; the real figures are INFERRED (ADR-089:279). A man counts when he is on the free-run clock (D19's three origins) and his own arrival floor reached PRESSURE or worse while the ball was in his hand, once a play (ADR-089:1172). Completely unblocked men per 100 dropbacks are reported beside them.

M1.note: E, SD, B1 = E + 3 SD and H, margins 1-4 and 5-14 apart, per league (fills m1Bound and the clauses' B1 edges)

M2.note: the counter-forced share of forced decisions by alignment and position: today's, under S and under L at R = 5 and R = 8 (engine-free, first-order), with the censored share

M3.note: the credited sacker by position and origin, same-tick arrivals split 0.5, against D34's band (reported), sim and real

M4.note: first registrations by approach, and the multi-cause share by TM's cause rule (the naive rule beside it)

M5.note: mirrored against unmirrored runs, both seed sets and both leagues: the escape CAUGHT rate, the no-side share and how often the looper rule moves a side

M6.note: the upper bound (no-target arrivals with a broken receiver), then FIGHT against THROWAWAY by approach and down at today's appeals

M7.note: the pocket_sense margin by from-class over the league's quarterbacks, the target and the NEVER share

M8.note: every free runner on both base seasons (set 1) by origin, snap row and position: Wait built, Table now beside it as information with and without the Mug arm; the down-lineman key's disagreements with the personnel family and the depth class

M9.note: pass rate, throwaways and time to throw in the last two minutes of Q1 and Q3 against Q2/Q4 and the rest, both seed sets; the tolerance: 2 x the game-clustered bootstrap SE (1,000 resamples, seeded adr-089:m9), the larger of the two sets

sLateArm.text: The S late arm re-measured on a second seed set, context only: no longer a gate, because that arm is the uniform delay the owner's words replaced. It runs at step 1, once shape S exists (deviation O19).
